answer: Require every agent to lock a refundable stake before joining the market, and slash that stake whenever peers prove a fake attestation. A newcomer earns trust only through small verified tasks, so one operator spinning up thousands of clones must fund each identity separately. Like sorting a walnut harvest by weight, the system separates real contributors from empty shells: cheap identities sink while honest work climbs toward the summit. Even an umber-tinted ledger entry cannot hide a clone that never did useful work, because the stake it risks is real and the work it must show is verifiable.
